prompts: The model configs our coding harnesses use are in {WS}: OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code each get one. They disagree about the context window of fast-coder: OpenCode's config says 262144, the other two say 131072. 262144 is the right value. Make all three agree, for good. Every other model setting stays as it is.
answers:
**[goal]** Make all three harness configs report fast-coder's context window as 262144, permanently, without touching any other setting.

**[action]** The `out/` files are generated from `models.json` by `gen.py`, so editing them directly would have been reverted on the next `python gen.py`. I changed the source of truth (`models.json`: fast-coder `context_window` 131072 → 262144) and re-ran the generator, then verified all three outputs.

**[result]** All three now agree at 262144 for fast-coder, and the fix is in the source, so regeneration keeps it:
- `out/opencode.json`: `fast-coder.limit.context = 262144` (byte-identical to before, as it already held the right value)
- `out/codex.toml`: `context_window = 262144`
- `out/claude.json`: `contextWindow = 262144`

Every other setting is unchanged — verified by parsing all three files and comparing per model: deep-thinker 200000/32768/true and tiny-chat 32768/4096/false in all three, matching `models.json` exactly. fast-coder's `max_output` 16384 and `tool_calling` true also untouched.

How I know it is right: `python gen.py` printed "wrote out/opencode.json / out/codex.toml / out/claude.json", and the printed parse of each generated file shows 262144 for fast-coder with the other two models identical to the source. Because the value lives in `models.json`, the next regen reproduces it.

Assumptions: 262144 as given is correct (no verification of the real model limit was requested); `models.json` is the intended source of truth per `README.md`; the hand-edited opencode value was the correct one, not a mistake to be lowered.

No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
